title: Diffusion & Adversarial Schrödinger Bridges via Iterative Proportional Markovian Fitting
claim: Two established iterative projection schemes alternate between different constraint sets; our combined scheme unifies them into one cycle converging to the same solution.
layout: 3 rows of Venn-diagram sequences, left-to-right arrows, shared legend on right
description: Three rows of Venn diagrams, each a sequence of states linked by projection arrows. Every diagram has three overlapping circles for the constraints p0/p1 marginals, the reciprocal class R and the Markov class M, and their intersection is labeled SB (Schrödinger Bridge). The top-left row shows IPF with two states, q^{2k+1} and q^{2k+2}, and arrows proj1 and proj0 between them. The top-right row shows IMF with arrows proj_M and proj_R. The bottom row shows the combined IPMF with four states, arrows proj1 (proj_M), proj_R, proj0 (proj_M), and a long return arrow proj_R looping back to the start. Green circles mean the object has the marginal. Orange circles mean it is in R or M. Grey circles mean it lacks the property. A legend sits at the far right. The eye goes first to the colored Venn diagrams, then follows the arrows.
caption: Diagrams of IPF, IMF, and unified IPMF procedure. All procedures aim to converge to the Schr¨odinger Bridge, i.e., a Markovian process in the reciprocal class, with marginals p0 and p1.
abstract: The Iterative Markovian Fitting (IMF) procedure, which iteratively projects onto the space of Markov processes and the reciprocal class, successfully solves the SchrÃ¶dinger Bridge (SB) problem. However, an efficient practical implementation requires a heuristic modification -- alternating between fitting forward and backward time diffusion at each iteration. This modification is crucial for stabilizing training and achieving reliable results in applications such as unpaired domain translation. Our work reveals a close connection between the modified version of IMF and the Iterative Proportional Fitting (IPF) procedure -- a foundational method for the SB problem, also known as Sinkhorn's algorithm. Specifically, we demonstrate that the heuristic modification of the IMF effectively integrates both IMF and IPF procedures. We refer to this combined approach as the Iterative Proportional Markovian Fitting (IPMF) procedure. Through theoretical and empirical analysis, we establish the convergence of the IPMF procedure under various settings, contributing to developing a unified framework for solving SB problems. Moreover, from a practical standpoint, the IPMF procedure enables a flexible trade-off between image similarity and generation quality, offering a new mechanism for tailoring models to specific tasks.
